title: Plan card sorts and tree tests
summary: Use card sorting for grouping and tree testing for findability, with separate measures and limits.
steps: For a card sort, define the grouping question, audience, understandable card set and open, closed or hybrid format. Check that the set represents the content question without requiring unexplained specialist terms.

Preserve original participant labels only in the approved source system; document any normalization, merges and co-placement denominators in an approved analysis. Participant-written labels may contain private text. Servant deliberately omits open-sort participant group names from its saved readout; do not paste them into an agent to recover detail.

The current runner does not automatically produce clusters or dendrograms. If a separate approved analysis proposes a structure from co-placement, treat it as a hypothesis to test, not proven navigation.

For a tree test, version the text hierarchies, write realistic neutral scenarios and specify every acceptable destination and scoring rule before fielding. Do not repeat the destination label in the task.

Define destination success, direct success, first-branch correctness, backtracks and timing separately. Self-reported ease or completion is a different measure. State the denominator for each rate and the treatment of missing paths.

The current readout supports destination success, directness, first-branch correctness when known and backtracks. Lostness is not automatically calculated; any separate lostness analysis needs a stated definition and valid path data.

Account for multiple tasks from the same person and any paired comparisons; they are not independent participants. Plan the primary comparison and any multiplicity handling rather than choosing the best-looking task afterward.

Test the resulting interface for remaining usability and accessibility questions. A successful text-tree destination does not demonstrate that people can find or use the same feature in the visual interface.
questions: Am I asking about grouping, findability or the finished interface?
Does the task wording disclose the answer?
Are private participant labels and dependent observations handled correctly?
example: Ask: You need to check what a letter sent last month asked you to do. Where would you look? Define the accepted destination in the scoring plan rather than naming that navigation item in the task.
